celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾: time, or what is after the declining of the sun until sunset, or the ʿAṣr prayer.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾: the species ﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ in his trade,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾, for they are not in loss, ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا﴾: enjoined one another ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾, that is, faith, ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ in obedience and away from disobedience.

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath. ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَفِي﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿في خُسْرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā) from الإنسان. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَتَواصَوْا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعَصْرِ): In al-Qāmūs he said: «al-ʿaṣr — with any of the three vowels [on the first letter], and with two ḍammas — is time (al-dahr); the plural is aʿṣār, ʿuṣūr, aʿṣur and ʿuṣur. Al-ʿaṣr is [also] the day and the night; the late afternoon until the reddening of the sun — and it may be vowelled [ʿaṣar]; the early morning; confinement; a small group; the clan; rain from the rain-clouds (al-muʿṣirāt); withholding; and a gift — ʿaṣarahu yaʿṣiruhu. And with the middle letter vowelled (al-ʿaṣar) it is a refuge and a place of safety, like al-ʿuṣr with ḍamma» — to the end of this long entry. If you say: what is meant by it here?
Ibn ʿAbbās said: it is time (al-dahr); Allah the Exalted swore by it because of the kinds of wonders in its passing. Qatāda said: al-ʿaṣr is the late afternoon; He swore by it as He swore by the forenoon (al-ḍuḥā), because of the proofs of [divine] power in both. It is also said that al-ʿaṣr is the day and the night, and from this is the saying of Ḥumayd ibn Thawr:
ولن يلبث العصران يوم وليلة ... إذا طلبا أن يدركا ما تيمما
(The two ʿaṣrs — a day and a night — do not delay, when they seek to attain what they have set out for.)
Muqātil said: al-ʿaṣr is the middle prayer; He swore by it. Al-Zamakhsharī began with this view, saying: «because of its excellence». Ibn Khālawayh said: «Sallām Abū al-Mundhir read "والعصِرِ" with kasra on the ṣād and the rāʾ. This occurs only in transferring the vowel on pausing, as when you say "مررت ببكر": the kasra of the rāʾ rises to the kāf on pausing. They do likewise with the nominative, but they do not transfer [the vowel] in the accusative except under poetic necessity. Sībawayh said: pausing on a noun is done in six ways: with ishmām, with ishbāʿ, with rawm of the vowel, with transfer of the vowel, with doubling, and with making [the letter] quiescent.» We say: ishmām is rounding the lips after making the letter quiescent, in the nominative and in what is indeclinable on ḍamma, to point to the vowel without a sound; its purpose is the distinction between the [originally] quiescent and the [letter] made quiescent in pausing [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «الفرق الساكن والمسكن», apparently with «بين» (between) dropped]. Rawm is pronouncing the vowel while weakening its sound; its purpose is the purpose of ishmām, except that it is more complete in clarity than ishmām, for the blind and the seeing perceive it, whereas ishmām is perceived only by the seeing.
(الْإِنْسانَ): a word applied to male and female of the children of Ādam. The Arabs sometimes made it feminine, saying insān and insāna. [The poet] said:
إنسانة تسقيك من إنسانها ... خمرا حلالا مقلتاها عنبه
(A woman who gives you to drink, from the pupil of her eye, a lawful wine — her eyeballs are its grapes.)
The «ال» in it is for comprehending the whole genus, so it includes the believer and the unbeliever, as is shown by the exception.
(خُسْرٍ): loss (ghabn). Al-khusr and al-khusrān are the same. In al-Miṣbāḥ he said: «Khasira in his trade khasāratan (with fatḥa), khusran and khusrānan; it is made transitive with the hamza, so one says akhsartuhu fīhā (I caused him to lose in it). And khasira khusran and khusrānan also [means]: he perished.»

* I'rab:
(وَالْعَصْرِ إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ): the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; «العصر» is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted verb of swearing. The clause «إن الإنسان ...» is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position. [It consists of] «إن» and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «في خسر», the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ): «إلا» is a particle of exception, and «الذين» is excepted from «الإنسان», because it is a generic noun, as preceded. The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; «عملوا الصالحات» is conjoined to «آمنوا»; «تواصوا بالحق» is also conjoined, i.e. they enjoined one another. It is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, [which was] dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). «تواصوا بالصبر» is also conjoined.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْعَصْرِ﴾.
It is time (الدهر); He swore by it.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾.
In punishment for his sins, and in losing his family and his dwelling in Paradise.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (إن الإنسان لفي خسر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «الذين»: accusative (manṣūb) as excepted from the generic noun {الإِنْسَانَ}.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (والعصر): it is an oath. The wāw is a substitute for the bāʾ, and its implied form is «ورب العصر» (by the Lord of the time); and likewise is the implied form in every oath by other than Allah. (العصر) is time (al-dahr).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (إلا الذين آمنوا): (الذين) is in the position of the accusative by exception from (الإنسان), because it has the meaning of the collective.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والعصر﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «العصر» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath, and the oath clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿الإنسان﴾: the noun (ism) of «إن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «في» is a preposition.
﴿خسر﴾: a noun genitive (majrūr) by ﴿في﴾, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the clause ﴿إن الإنسان لفي خسر﴾ is the answer of the oath, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā).
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿وعملوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «عملوا» is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause ﴿عملوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿الصالحات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿عملوا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra, because it is a sound feminine plural.
﴿وتواصوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause ﴿تواصوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿بالحق﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «الحق» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تواصوا﴾.
﴿وتواصوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause ﴿تواصوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿بالصبر﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «الصبر» is a noun genitive by the bāʾ, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تواصوا﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The implied form is: by the Lord of al-ʿaṣr. Everything that is called ʿaṣr is included in it, because no specification has occurred on which a proof can stand: al-ʿaṣr is time (al-dahr), al-ʿaṣr is the late afternoon (al-ʿashiyy), and al-ʿaṣr is refuge.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: الإنسان is in the sense of "people", and al-khusr (loss) is entering the Fire, which is the greatest loss.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: الَّذِينَ is in the position of an exception from an affirmative (statement); آمَنُوا is its ṣila (relative clause), and likewise وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ, because it is conjoined.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(والعصر) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". (اللام) is the lām of oath, a substitute for the shifted lām. (إلّا) is for exception. (الذين) is a relative in the position of accusative as the excepted. (بالحقّ) is attached to (تواصوا); (بالصبر) is attached to the second (تواصوا). Clause: « (أقسم) بالعصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «إنّ الإنسان لفي خسر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the oath.
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «تواصوا (الأولى) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «تواصوا (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(العصر): a noun meaning time (dahr), or the time after the decline of the sun until sunset, or the ʿaṣr prayer; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The generic (jinsiyya) (ال) and the specific-reference (ʿahdiyya) (ال):
The generic (ال) is either for the inclusion of all individuals, as in His saying, the Exalted (إن الإنسان لفي خسر), i.e. the whole genus of man;
or for the inclusion of the qualities of the individuals, as in: (زيد الرجل كرما), i.e. the one perfect in the quality of generosity.
And the (ال) of specific reference: either its referent is something previously mentioned, as in His saying, the Exalted (كما أرسلنا إلى فرعون رسولا فعصى فرعون الرسول), or something known in the mind, as in His saying, the Exalted (إذ هما في الغار).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {والعصر}: the majority read with sukūn on the ṣād. Sallām read «والعَصِرْ» and «والصَّبِرْ» with kasra on the ṣād and the bāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is not permissible except in pause, by transferring the vowel." It is reported from Abū ʿAmr «بالصَّبِر» with kasra on the bāʾ, as an ishmām (partial vowel sound). "This too is not permissible except in pause," end of quotation. A group transmitted this reading, such as al-Hudhalī, Abū l-Faḍl al-Rāzī and Ibn Khālawayh. Al-Hudhalī said: "«والعَصِرْ» and «والصَّبِرْ», «والفَجِرْ», «والوَتِرْ»: the letter before the quiescent letter is given a kasra in all of these by Hārūn and Ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAmr; the rest read them with sukūn, like the generality." End of quotation. So he gives this reading without restriction, in both pause and running speech. Ibn Khālawayh said: "«والصَّبِرْ» with transfer of the vowel, from Abū ʿAmr", and he too gave it without restriction. Abū l-Faḍl said: "ʿĪsā of Basra read «بالصَّبِرْ», transferring the vowel of the rāʾ to the bāʾ; one need not bring some part of the vowel in pause, nor make it quiescent, which would bring two quiescent letters together; this is a widespread dialect, not irregular but well attested, and it is an indication of case-ending (iʿrāb), a separation from the meeting of two quiescents, and a rendering of the due of what is paused on, namely quiescence." End of quotation. This suggests what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, that it ought to be so. And they recited on this:
4636 -. . . . . . واصْطِفاقاً بالرِّجِلْ ... يريد بالرِّجْلِ
(. . . and clapping with the foot.) He means «بالرِّجْلِ». And another said:
4637 - أنا جريرٌ كُنْيتي أبو عَمِرْ ... أَضْرِبُ بالسَّيْفِ وسَعْدٌ في القَصِرْ
(I am Jarīr, my kunya is Abū ʿAmr; I strike with the sword while Saʿd is in the palace.)
Transfer is also permissible with ḍamma, as in his saying:
4638 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . إذْ جَدَّ النُّقُرْ ...
(. . . when the drumming became earnest.)
And al-ʿaṣr means the night and the day. He said:
4639 - ولن يَلْبَثَ العَصْرانِ يَوْمٌ وليلةٌ ... إذا طلبا أن يُدْرِكا ما تَيَمَّما
(The two ʿaṣrs, a day and a night, will not delay when they seek to overtake what they aim at.)

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {إِنَّ الإنسان}: what is meant by it is generality, by the evidence of the exception made from it, which is one of the proofs of generality. The majority read «لَفي خُسْرٍ» with sukūn on the sīn; Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Hurmuz and ʿĀṣim, in one report, with ḍamma on it, like al-ʿusr and al-yusr, both of which were treated at the beginning of this work, in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ (٣)).
The majority read the bāʾ of «الصَّبْرِ» with sukūn, while some read it with a kasra; this follows the dialect of those who, in pause, transfer the ḍamma and the kasra to the vowelless letter before it, out of concern to make the case ending (iʿrāb) clear.

zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-ʿAṣr
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والعَصْرِ﴾ ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ﴾ ("by time, the human being is surely in loss"): "the human being" here is in the sense of ”اَلنّاسُ“ ("people"), as you say ”قَدْ كَثُرَ الدِّرْهَمُ، والدِّينارُ في أيْدِي النّاسِ“ ("the dirham and the dinar have become plentiful in people's hands"), meaning "the dirhams have become plentiful".
And His saying: ﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾: ”اَلْخُسْرُ“ and ”اَلْخُسْرانُ“ have one meaning. The meaning is: "People who are unbelievers and who act without obedience to Allah are surely in loss."

zajjaj:3-3.t:
﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ وتَواصَوْا بِالحَقِّ وتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ ("except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience"): they enjoin one another to remain steadfast upon Allah's oneness and belief in His Prophet, peace be upon him; ﴿وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾: upon obedience to Allah, striving (jihād) in His way, and upholding the laws of His Prophet. And ”اَلْعَصْرُ“ is time (al-dahr), and ”اَلْعَصْرانِ“ are the day and the night. The poet said:
وَلَنْ يَلْبَثَ العَصْرانِ يَوْمٌ ولَيْلَةٌ ∗∗∗ إذا طَلَبا أنْ يُدْرِكا ما تَيَمَّما
(The two times — a day and a night — will not linger long when they seek to attain what they have aimed at.)
﴿والعَصْرِ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 1] is an oath, and its answer is ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 2]. Some said its meaning is "by the Lord of time", as He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23] ("so by the Lord of the heaven and the earth").
